answer_summary: F: 1,4-dihydroxycyclohexa-2,5-diene from addition of 4-lithio-4'-(TBSO)biphenyl to the drawn p-quinol carbonyl (biphenyl arm at C1, 4-bromophenyl at C4), C30H33BrO3Si. G: both tertiary OH of F capped as OTES (aryl ether shown as OTES; TBS/TES are formula-identical C6H15Si), C42H61BrO3Si3. H: LiOH cleaves only the aryl silyl ether, liberating the free phenol on the remote biphenyl ring while both tertiary OTES survive, C36H47BrO3Si2 (matches the problem-printed formula). I: PhI(OAc)2/H2O two-electron oxidative dearomatization converts the phenol into a para-quinol (cyclohexa-2,5-dienone; sp3 junction bearing the new OH from H2O), C36H47BrO4Si2. J: addition of drawn 4-lithiobromobenzene to the dienone C=O gives a 1,4-dihydroxy diene ring bearing the new 4-bromophenyl arm, C42H52Br2O4Si2. K: both new OH capped as OTES (four OTES, two aryl bromides), C54H80Br2O4Si4. L: Ni(COD)2/2,2'-bipyridine Yamamoto macrocyclization joins the two aryl bromides by one new biaryl bond, closing the five-ring para-linked belt, C54H80O4Si4 (matches the problem-printed formula). Final drawn step (TBAF then SnCl2) gives the boxed [5]CPP = five para-linked benzenes, C30H20 with five aromatic 6pi systems, used as endpoint consistency check.
assumptions: Molecules are encoded as explicit finite molecular graphs (six-carbon ring units, per-atom hydrogen counts, sp3/sp2 status, substituents, Kekule double bonds, inter-ring biaryl links); all requested properties are computed over these graphs by decide.

Standard general chemistry is used only as trusted general law: aryllithium 1,2-addition to ketones; silyl protection of alcohols with TESCl/imidazole; comparative hydrolytic lability of aryl vs tertiary-alkyl silyl ethers under LiOH (selectivity pinned by the printed formula of H); PhI(OAc)2/H2O oxidative dearomatization of phenols to para-quinols (the problem explicitly states PhI(OAc)2 is a two-electron oxidant and the same transformation produces the drawn starting material); Ni(0)/2,2'-bipyridine Yamamoto aryl-aryl homocoupling of aryl bromides; TBAF desilylation; SnCl2 reductive aromatization (both reagents and the boxed [5]CPP product are given in the problem).
Aromatic/antiaromatic ring counts follow Huckel's rule (4n+2 aromatic, 4n for a closed p-loop antiaromatic), proved arithmetically in the file.
Integer atomic masses C=12, H=1, O=16, Si=28, Br=80, Li=7, consistent with the 6.4 instruction to use integer atomic masses.
In structure G the aryl silyl ether is recorded as OTES; TBS and TES contribute identical formulas (C6H15Si), so this choice is formula-neutral and does not affect the printed anchor formula of H.
source_gaps: The problem asks only to draw structures and prints no stereochemical template for F-L; the two new quaternary carbinol centres in F, J (and retained in G, K, L) are therefore fixed constitutionally (explicit sp3 centres in the encoding) with no specified absolute or relative configuration.

Whether the aryl silyl ether in G remains TBS or is exchanged to TES is not distinguishable by any printed data (identical C6H15Si formula); the formalization records it as OTES per the drawn TESCl legend, and notes the equivalence explicitly.

The exact proton-count bookkeeping of the NaH deprotonation steps (which OH is transiently deprotonated) is not printed; the formalization encodes the neutral isolated products F and J, with the NaH step noted in the natural-language answer and in derivation comments.
